thread:
Maya: Heads up — I ran a quick experiment stacking coarse (16-token) and fine (4-token) prefetch windows in our hybrid speculative pipeline. Curious if others have tried this pattern.
Sam: Nice. what's the exact stack? 16 then 4 or adaptive?
Maya: 16 then 4. idea: coarse prefetch covers majority of KV reuse, fine handles tail. Config used: prefetch_windows=[16,4], priority=LRU, early_exit_threshold=0.8
Leo: Results?
Maya: Baseline (single 8): p50 latency 42ms, tokens/s 320; stacked: p50 38ms (-9.5%), tokens/s 350 (+9.4%). PPL on eval set +0.6 (worse).
Tara: Small quality hit. Which eval set?
Maya: mix of instr-follow (3k prompts) + conv snippets. Automated embedding-sim drop ~0.8%
Sam: Could be due to cache staleness when fine window overwrites coarse entries — did you pin kv tags per prefix?
Maya: No. I used naive eviction. Will try pinning identifiers. Also suspect scheduling: tight mixing increased concurrency leading to more partial prefixes in KV.
Leo: Any logs? paste sample?
Maya: Snippet: 
```json
{"prefetch_windows": [16,4], "kv_policy": "naive_eviction"}
```
and a sample trace: `trace: prefetch16->hit, prefetch4->miss -> backend fetch`
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary infra job started for 1755559999-stack-prefetch-tryout
Sam: If we pin coarse entries and mark fine as ephemeral, maybe no overwrite. Also try time-decayed weights: prioritize coarse for >32 tokens.
Maya: Good plan. Running 2nd pass with pinned coarse and kv-tagging. Also adding a quality eval: 5k long-form summaries and human spot-check.
Tara: What's acceptance criteria? Latency >5% and quality drop <0.3% sim?
Sam: I'd set soft thresholds: latency improvement >=5% AND sim loss <=0.4%. Otherwise roll back.
Maya: Run commands I'm using: 
```bash
./run_bench --model redwood-7b --batch 8 --prefetch 16,4 --kv-policy naive --eval ./evalsets/mix3k.json
```
Next run: 
```bash
./run_bench --model redwood-7b --batch 8 --prefetch 16,4 --kv-policy pin-coarse --eval ./evalsets/longform5k.json
```
Leo: :thumbsup: ping me when second run done, I'll help analyze model logits for bias.
Maya: Will do. Expect results in ~2h. if quality holds we can wire this into hybrid default.
Tara: Note: include A/B with speculative fallback disabled to isolate prefetch effect.
Maya: Good catch. I'll run A/B variants.
Sam: One more: record token-level timing and kv hit rate split by window size. That helped before.
Maya: Will log kv_hit_by_window in next run. Thanks.
